Carnitine acyltransferase I (CAT I) is the enzyme that catalyses the reaction of an Acyl-CoA molecule with carnitine, forming Acylcarnitine.  CAT I is located on the outer mitochondrial membrane and once Acylcarnitine has been formed, it can be transported across the mitochondrial membrane via the carrier protein Carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase.  CAT II is located on the inner mitochondrial membrane and catalyses the reaction of Acylcarnitine with carnitine, reforming Acyl-CoA and carnitine.  The Acyl-CoA is now in the matrix and can be used in beta-oxidation.

The correct answer is the quadruple test. This is because this woman has a BMI over 30kg/m2 which means that there is a risk of inaccurate results with the combined test and NIFTY. Sanger et al (2002) showed that women with a BMI of 30kg/m2 or above have a 12% false positive rate with the combined test and a 15% false positive rate with NIFTY. The quadruple test is the most accurate of the biochemical screening tests and therefore is the best option in this situation. Amniocentesis and CVS are diagnostic, not screening tests.  Sanger, A., Fuhrman, E. R., Shen, Y., Zhang, Y., Wang, Y., Wang, J., ... & Zhang, Y. (2002). "Evaluation of the accuracy of serum alpha-fetoprotein, unconjugated oestriol, human chorionic gonadotropin and inhibin-A in Down syndrome screening in obese pregnant women". American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology, 186(5), 371-378.

Agranulocytosis is a severe form of neutropenia characterised by low numbers of granulocytes on the blood count. This can be asymptomatic or present with recurrent life-threatening infections; in severe cases can be associated with0.3-0.5% mortality rate.  More commonly patients will present with fever, muscle weakness and a sore mouth and with bleeding gums.  Apo-proteins I and V are also commonly decreased. Clozapine is a drug associated with agranulocytosis and other bone marrow suppressive effects including neutropenia and thrombocytopaenia.
